title: Noise-to-Signal Spill (Debug Logs in Production)
pattern: Presence of active `debug!` or `trace!` log statements inside hot code paths without a mechanism for build-time or compile-time stripping.
why_bad: At scale, high-frequency logging creates immense noise, increases CPU/IO overhead significantly, fills filesystems, and risks exfiltrating sensitive PII into log systems [83, 282, 691].
detection: A static analyzer detecting active debug-level or trace-level macros within functions annotated as hot paths or loops, or lacking static stripping gates.
counterexample:
Using compile-time features or log gates:
```rust
#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
log::debug!("Processing token segment: {}", packet.user_id);
```
fix: Strip verbose trace and debug logs from production builds entirely using build-time feature gates (such as cargo features targeting maximum log levels like `max_level_info`).
